title: Bounded loop from an invariant
statement: Let a program, depth bound, condition $c$, body $s$, initial state $\sigma$, postcondition $Q$, invariant predicates $I_i$ on states for natural numbers $i$, iteration count $n\in\mathbb N$, and per-iteration bounds $b_i\in\mathbb N$ be given. If $I_0$ holds at $\sigma$, then for every $i<n$, every state satisfying $I_i$ has a safe condition that holds and admits an execution of $s$ within time $b_i$ to a state satisfying $I_{i+1}$. If every state satisfying $I_n$ has a safe condition that does not hold and satisfies $Q$, then the loop with condition $c$ and body $s$ ends in a state satisfying $Q$ within time $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\bigl((\operatorname{cost}(c)+1+b_i)+(\operatorname{cost}(c)+1)\bigr)$.
hypotheses_covered: The invariant $I_0$ holds at the initial state
For every $i<n$ and state satisfying $I_i$, the condition is safe and holds, and the body reaches a state satisfying $I_{i+1}$ within $b_i$
For every state satisfying $I_n$, the condition is safe and false and $Q$ holds
